summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47% QoQ to INR4,282 million and EBITDA reached INR919 million, while management reiterated the FY28 target of US$400 million revenue at ~40% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sharp sequential recovery after a weak Q3, driven by the start of invoicing for drug-device combinations (DDC) and the India Semaglutide launch at the end of the quarter. Full-year revenue fell 2% YoY to INR14,216 million and EBITDA fell about 35%, both hit by delayed Semaglutide approvals. Management deferred the Steriscience injectables and Brooks merger scheme, citing smaller-investor valuation concerns and a lower listed-company share price, and said it will revisit in about two years. Capacity expansion remains on track, with a new DDC line expected to be available from next quarter and three lines installed by end FY27.

segments.name: DDC (drug-device combinations) / Semaglutide
segments.commentary: Invoicing began this year; Canada approvals received for two partners, and shipments to both Canadian partners have commenced. Current line is fully committed back-to-back, and the new 500-litre-capable line is expected to be available from next quarter.

segments.name: Injectables and soft gelatin (base business)
segments.commentary: Signed 10 new licences, launched 15-plus products and added customers during the year. Soft gelatin capacity is expected to be fully utilised within the current period, and a fourth injectable line is coming in unit two.

segments.name: Biologics (nascent)
segments.commentary: Funnel expanded almost 4x YoY; a European biosimilar partner, a US biosimilar major and a second animal-health project from a top-three global player were added. Management expects a meaningful contribution in FY28 and commercial manufacturing from FY29; no revenue or EBITDA split was disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY28 guidance reiterated: US$400 million organic revenue at around 40% EBITDA margin; FY27 guidance not given beyond expecting a strong year and a sequential improvement in revenue and EBITDA each quarter.
Working capital is expected to normalise during FY27 after elevated levels this year.
Soft gelatin and injectables trending close to the US$100 million mark, with further growth expected.
Saudi Arabia Semaglutide launch described as imminent, now that freedom to operate is in place.
Scheme with Steriscience injectables and Brooks deferred; to be revisited in about two years if strategic intent holds.
capex_capacity: Part of a US$100 million capex programme; the new line installed a couple of months ago is in qualification and expected to be available from Q1 FY27 (next quarter), with commercial availability in Q2.
Two additional lines are planned this year, giving three lines by end FY27; a fourth injectable line is coming in unit two.

Existing line capped at 200-litre batch size; new lines can go to 500 litres, and up to 750-1,000 litres in the longer term. Moving from 200 to 500 litres raises output about 2.5x (about 60,000 pens/day at 200 litres).
Sterile manufacturing capacity framed as about 225 sterile days per line, roughly 675 days across three lines.
Capacity expansion fully funded through incremental domestic and international bank borrowings; the company added about 400 people at its flagship site.
demand_pricing: Management says demand exceeds supply for at least the next two years; customers have reserved capacity with upfront fees and take-or-pay contracts.
India Semaglutide: partners were present on day one across multiple brands, and the customer base holds almost two-thirds of the Indian generic market by value as of end April.
The company is first and only CDMO for the first three generic Semaglutide approvals in US and Canada; ANVISA approval received, positioning it for Brazil.
Brazil is said to be the largest market outside North America for Semaglutide; no Brazil market-size numbers were given. CDMO terms are ex-works, so tariffs fall on customers.
Oral Semaglutide seen as taking 25% to one-third of the market, with injectables remaining dominant.
Customer advances broadly unchanged from the INR250 crore reported last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Brazil local-manufacturing duty risk and whether profit-share arrangements exist with other regulated-market customers.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 28% duty applies only where local manufacturing exists, which it does not yet in Brazil, and CDMO terms are ex-works. It declined to discuss customer-specific profit-share terms beyond what was public.

qa_highlights.question: Why inventories rose from INR158 crore (March 2025) to INR440 crore (March 2026) for a service provider.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the inventory is customer-funded and fungible, pooled across customers, and is adjusted against customer advances with no material P&L risk; the P&L impact is limited to conversion fees.

qa_highlights.question: Why opex and staff costs rose despite lower revenue.
qa_highlights.answer: Opex is supporting the capacity expansion ahead of the second and third DDC lines, which underpins the FY28 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of DDC capacity and utilisation.
qa_highlights.answer: The new line is available from next quarter and will ease pressure on the existing line; three lines are expected by end FY27, and the sequential revenue and EBITDA improvement is tied to these additions.

qa_highlights.question: Biologics contribution timing and profitability.
qa_highlights.answer: Agreements are expected over FY27 and FY28, with a meaningful contribution in FY28 and commercial manufacturing from FY29. Management declined to give biologics revenue or EBITDA-loss figures.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year FY27 numbers and Canadian approvals for other clients.
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated FY28 guidance only and gave no FY27 figures. It said more Canadian approvals are expected over the next few quarters but could not give a timeline.

risks_watch: Timing of the new DDC line qualification and commissioning in Q1/Q2 FY27, and whether revenue ramps sequentially as guided.
Brazil and other emerging-market approvals, and the pace at which partners get them.
Biologics contracts are still at an early stage and commercial manufacturing is FY29 onwards; execution risk on the FY28 contribution.
Working capital and inventory build (customer-funded), with normalisation expected in FY27.
Dropped Steriscience and Brooks scheme deferred; governance optics given the reduced shareholder support.
Customer concentration and confidentiality limit disclosure of segment and customer-level economics.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, approvals and the FY28 target, but evasive on segment economics, biologics profitability, FY27 numbers and customer terms, citing confidentiality. The Steriscience/Brooks deferral was framed as a governance-driven decision.

Goodwill is a non-cash item and does not have any bearing on the operational performance and liquidity of the company.
I'm just staying put with three lines which will be ready and which will be visible by end of FY27.
